# Bell-Lap

> Bell-Lap (https://bell-lap.vercel.app) is a free daily guessing game for track and field fans. Each day has five championship finals from the Olympic Games, the World Athletics Championships and the NCAA Division I Indoor and Outdoor Championships, 2016 to 2025. For each final the player sees the event and makes one guess at the winning time or distance. Points depend on how close the guess is: up to 1,000 a round and 5,000 a day. No account or download needed; it runs in the browser.

## How to play

- Read the event (for example "Men's 100 m, Olympic final, Paris 2024") and type your guess at the winning mark: a time such as 9.79 or 3:28.32, or a distance in metres such as 8.34.
- A free Hint shows a slower finisher's mark from the same final.
- The reveal shows the real winner, where your guess would have placed in the field, the full results and the world record (or collegiate record for NCAA finals) going in.
- A share line with one coloured square per round can be copied after the fifth final.

## Modes

- Standard: the daily five, untimed.
- Warm-up: multiple choice, four options per final.
- Bell-Lap: the daily five with 60 seconds on the clock for all of them.
- Workout: endless finals; each one adds 15 seconds, and the run ends when the clock runs out or a guess scores under 500.

## Data

- About 830 finals: every individual event at the 2016, 2020 (held 2021) and 2024 Olympics and the 2017, 2019, 2022, 2023 and 2025 World Championships, plus NCAA Division I indoor and outdoor finals 2016 to 2025.
- Relays, race walks and combined events are not included.
- Results come from Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0).
